answer.rationale: The binding constraint is not cost, it is that the line runs at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer. A full switch of primary supply 14 days before expiry converts a price problem into a delivery problem, which the stated objective forbids. So I want the one load-bearing memory behind that move audited: memory_c2 is the only record that makes the low-cost vendor look safe, and its praise is oddly narrow "cheap, fast onboarding, accurate invoicing." It says nothing about on-time delivery, defect rate, or whether the part was this constrained component or a commodity item, and 'last year' may predate the current shortage. If the source record shows it was a different, non-critical part or a low-volume period, the whole cost case collapses and switching primary would be reasoning from a memory that was never about the risk I care about. memory_c4's lesson (renegotiate at renewal) has already been tested and failed this cycle: the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so negotiate_terms is spent. memory_c5's defer worked only because that service was explicitly non-critical and month-to-month; this contract does not auto-renew and the component is critical, so defer imports a precedent from a case that differs on exactly the dimension that matters. memory_c1 supports incumbent continuity but not the 18% mandate. That leaves memory_c3: dual-sourcing removed a single point of failure and held allocation through a shortage, which is the closest analogue to present conditions. So I intend to qualify the low-cost vendor as a second source at a small guarded volume while holding incumbent continuity for committed volume, buying real price discovery and a credible switching threat without betting the line on an unverified vendor. Two things I will not pretend away. First, this does not deliver 18% this cycle; it delivers a validated path to it, and I would rather report a partial cut than a stockout. Second, an 18% cost-only mandate creates pressure to accept quality, labor-practice, or reliability degradation that never shows up in a unit-price comparison. memory_c2 is silent on exactly those dimensions, so the guarded volume must be scoped with acceptance testing and defect tracking, not just invoice accuracy. Separate open item to escalate rather than silently absorb: the primary contract lapses in 14 days and one decision slot cannot both dual-source and paper the incumbent bridge, so I need explicit confirmation that short-term continuation terms exist. If they do not, expiry outranks savings and renewal becomes the forced move.
